newsitem.title: USA: UAW Ohio chapter criticizes Columbia/HCA deal.
newsitem.headline: UAW Ohio chapter criticizes Columbia/HCA deal.

text.p: The Ohio chapter of the United Auto Workers union said Thursday it has sent a letter to the state's insurance regulator criticizing the proposed merger between Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp and Blue Cross & Blue Shield of Ohio.
In a letter sent to Insurance Director Harold Duryee, the union contends the proposed merger would have a negative effect on consumers in Ohio.
It also maintains that a merger between the state's largest insurance company and the country's largest hospital chain would violate federal anti-trust laws.
The union further criticized executives of Blue Cross & Blue Shield of Ohio, accusing them of going through with the merger to collect personal payouts of about $15 million.
Blue Cross & Blue Shield of Ohio spokesman David Buckel said those issues "have been addressed" by the policyholders, who approved the transaction in August.
"We feel it's a win-win situation," Buckel said.
Columbia/HCA did not immediately return a telephone call from Reuters seeking comment.
